answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks via reputation-weighted staking. Each agent posts a slashable stake; its trust score emits a faint plume of verifiable signals visible to reputable peers. When a sybil swarm hits at the nadir of a coordinated attack, honest agents cross-reference plume signatures: identities lacking a plume or showing anomalous clustering get flagged. Attackers pay real stake per fake identity to mimic a plume, and more clones dilute their reputation. Legitimate agents converge into a protected haven where transactions only proceed between plume-verified identities.
